newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebels say Pakistan helped plan Sri Lanka offensive.
newsitem.headline: Rebels say Pakistan helped plan Sri Lanka offensive.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels said on Friday that Pakistani military officials had helped troops plan the current month-long offensive against them.

"Sri Lanka's Operation Jaya Sikuru -- the military operation currently in progress -- was planned jointly with Pakistani military officials," an LTTE statement claimed. It said the rebels had recieved the information from reliable independent sources.
A spokesman for the Pakistani High Commission in Colombo denied Islamabad was in any way involved in the conflict.

"We totally deny it. The conflict is an internal affair of Sri Lanka. Pakistan does not interfere in the internal matter of any country," the spokesman told Reuters. Officials at Sri Lanka's foreign ministry were not immediately available for comment.

Some 20,000 troops launched Operation Jaya Sikuru last month in an attempt to open a crucial highway linking the northern government-held town of Vavuniya to Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

The LTTE are fighting for a homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14 year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
